column.whereHint: Sentry's culprit - the function, route, or file the error was attributed to. Long paths are shortened; the linked issue has the full text.
column.eventsHint: Events recorded for this issue inside the selected date range, not its lifetime total.
column.usersHint: Distinct users who hit this issue inside the selected date range.
column.lastSeenHint: When Sentry last recorded an event for this issue.

sentry.empty: No unresolved issue recorded any events in this range.
sentry.truncated: Sentry had more than the {n} issues listed. They are the ones with the most events, and the totals above count only those - narrow the date range for a complete picture.
sentry.needsAuth: Add a Sentry auth token under Connectors (or set the SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN env var) to see your issues.
sentry.tokenRejected: Sentry rejected the token for {label}. Auth tokens expire and can be revoked - create a new one under Sentry Settings -> Account -> User Auth Tokens and paste it in under Connectors.
sentry.missingScopes: Sentry won't let the {label} token read issues. It needs the org:read, project:read and event:read scopes, and event:read is the one that returns the issue stream. Recreate the token with all three under Sentry Settings -> Account -> User Auth Tokens.
sentry.orgTokenKind: The token for {label} is a Sentry organization auth token (sntrys_...). Those exist for CI - uploading releases and source maps - and carry no event:read, so there is no scope to tick that would let this one read issues. Replace it with a user auth token from Sentry Settings -> Account -> User Auth Tokens.
sentry.badUrl: {url} doesn't answer as a Sentry API for {label}. Use https://sentry.io, your region host (https://de.sentry.io), or the origin of your self-hosted install - the part of the URL before /organizations/.
sentry.noOrgs: The token for {label} can't see any Sentry organizations. Either it lacks the org:read scope or the account belongs to none. If you'd rather not grant org:read, name the organizations explicitly under Connectors.
sentry.orgsFailed: Sentry doesn't recognize {orgs} for this token. Check the slug under Connectors - it's the part of your Sentry URL after /organizations/ - or clear the field to use every organization the token can see.
sentry.orgsPartial: Excludes {orgs}: Sentry doesn't recognize them for this token. The numbers below cover the remaining organizations only.

setup.noAccounts: No Sentry connections yet. Add one to start tracking issues.
setup.tokenHelp: A user auth token with org:read, project:read and event:read. Create one under Sentry Settings -> Account -> User Auth Tokens.
setup.tokenWarning: Organization tokens (sntrys_...) are built for CI and cannot read issues - fastdash will tell you so if you paste one.
setup.baseUrlHelp: Leave this as it is for sentry.io. Use https://de.sentry.io if your organization is pinned to the EU region, or your own origin for a self-hosted install.
setup.orgsPlaceholder: acme-inc, my-team - leave empty for all
setup.orgsHelp: The slug from your Sentry URL, the part after /organizations/. Leave it empty to report on every organization the token can see.
